name: Content-Level Because Adjunct

1.definition: Presents a circumstance as the reason for the event or state asserted.

examples.form: Jo left [because the room was too cold].

projection.target: The cold explains the leaving on the content reading. In the reasoning use of because, its clause can instead supply evidence for making the assertion.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Because giving the reason for an event
curious.summary: A because-part can give the reason that something happened or was the case.
curious.body:
In Jo left because the room was too cold, the because-part says why Jo left. The cold explains the leaving. This is the content reading: the circumstance is presented as the reason for the event or state asserted.

Because has another use, in reasoning. There the because-part can give evidence for making the statement, not an explanation for an event.

examples.text: Jo left [because the room was too cold].
We stayed inside [because it was raining].

curious.try: Say Jo left because the room was too cold. What happened, and what is the reason it happened?

teacher.summary: Useful for separating because as a reason for an event from because as evidence for a claim.
teacher.explain: In the content use, a PP headed by because with a finite clause as its complement modifies the predication and presents a circumstance as the reason for the event or state asserted. In Jo left because the room was too cold, the cold explains the leaving. In the reasoning use, the because-clause can instead supply evidence for making the assertion. This dictionary covers the content reading; the evidential use has its own entry.
teacher.terms: Adverbial clause of reason: the traditional name. In this grammar because heads a PP whose complement is a finite clause.

examples.text: Jo left [because the room was too cold].

contrasts.text: Jo left because the room was too cold.
We stayed inside because it was raining.
contrasts.note: The rain is the reason for staying inside.

watch_for: A learner might read every because-clause as explaining the event, when a reasoning use gives evidence for an assertion.
A learner might take the because-clause as a separate sentence, when it modifies the predication.
teacher.activity: Students complete sentence starters like Jo left because and We stayed inside because. They underline the reason and say which event or state it explains.

child.explain: Because tells the reason something happened. Jo left because the room was too cold. The cold is why Jo left.

examples.text: Jo left [because the room was too cold].
We stayed inside [because it was raining].

child.play: Start a sentence with I wore a coat because. Ask a friend to finish it with a reason. Then swap.
